question: Determine the values of the constants $a$ and $b$ for which the function $$f(x)=\begin{cases}3x+1, & x\leq 1\\ ax+b, & 1<x<3\\ 2x+5, & x\geq 3\end{cases}$$ is continuous for all real values of $x$, and justify your conclusion using the conditions of continuity at the joining points.
explanation:
Required Condition
Each expression defining $f$ is a polynomial and hence is continuous in its respective interval. Therefore, continuity needs to be examined only at the joining points $x=1$ and $x=3$.

For continuity at $x=1$, we require $$\lim_{x\to1^-}f(x)=f(1)=\lim_{x\to1^+}f(x).$$ From the first branch, $$f(1)=3(1)+1=4$$ and $$\lim_{x\to1^-}f(x)=4.$$ From the middle branch, $$\lim_{x\to1^+}f(x)=a+b.$$ Hence, continuity at $x=1$ gives $$a+b=4.$$

For continuity at $x=3$, we require $$\lim_{x\to3^-}f(x)=f(3)=\lim_{x\to3^+}f(x).$$ From the middle branch, $$\lim_{x\to3^-}f(x)=3a+b.$$ Since the third branch applies at $x=3$, $$f(3)=2(3)+5=11$$ and $$\lim_{x\to3^+}f(x)=11.$$ Therefore, $$3a+b=11.$$

Solving the Conditions
Subtracting $a+b=4$ from $3a+b=11$, we obtain $$2a=7,$$ so $$a=\frac{7}{2}.$$ Substituting in $a+b=4$, $$\frac{7}{2}+b=4,$$ giving $$b=\frac{1}{2}.$$

Final Result
Thus, for $$a=\frac{7}{2},\qquad b=\frac{1}{2},$$ the values and limits agree at both joining points. Since each individual branch is continuous elsewhere, the given function is continuous for all real $x$.
